page: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance deployed on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is equipped with an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at a base clock speed of 3.9 GHz, featuring 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs via hyperthreading. System memory comprises 128.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance relies on burstable CPU allocation and lacks attached local storage. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 15 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included. Processor extension flags include AVX-512, AMX int8 and tile matrix acceleration, SHA-NI, and VAES.

Benchmark testing reveals strong multi-core execution capabilities and memory read throughput. The instance recorded a Clang software compilation score of 58924.0 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 436.31 GB/sec, placing both results in top tier benchmark categories. Static web serving throughput reached 104.85 GB/sec, while LLM prompt processing for a medium 7B model achieved 303.91 tokens per second. Uncached memory read bandwidth measured 196.96 GB/sec. However, large block uncached memory write operations achieved 82.79 GB/sec, placing write throughput in the middle performance tier.

The combination of 64 burstable vCPUs and DDR5 memory provides high compute density tailored for variable workloads, maximizing resource utilization efficiency over sustained full-core allocations. Integrated AMX and AVX-512 hardware extensions allow acceleration of matrix math and cryptographic functions without requiring dedicated GPU hardware. Recommended workload fits include multi-threaded software compilation, CI/CD build automation, static web serving, redis key-value stores, and CPU-based machine learning prompt processing.
description: Amazon Web Services c8i-flex.16xlarge is a compute-optimized x86_64 instance running on the Nitro hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor at 3.9 GHz, it features 32 physical cores, 64 vCPUs, and a burstable CPU allocation mode. The system includes 128.0 GB of DDR5 RAM at 7 GHz, a 480 MB L3 cache, and 15 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with no attached local storage. Built-in instruction sets include Intel AMX and AVX-512 for accelerated matrix and vector calculations. Benchmark performance shows top tier results for software compilation with Clang, multi-core Geekbench benchmarks, and static web serving throughput at 104.85 GB/sec. Uncached memory read throughput reaches 196.96 GB/sec, though memory write speeds remain in average performance ranges. This instance fits multi-threaded software compilation, build automation pipelines, medium LLM prompt processing, and high-throughput static web serving.
